profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.East Building 3, sits on the Intergate.East sub-campus and is listed by aggregator DatacenterHawk at 3333 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168. That same source labeled this one listing "120th Street" rather than "Place," unlike its neighboring Building 2, 4, and 5 listings, which is treated here as a likely source-side typo rather than silently corrected, since Place is the more probable reading given the pattern in the source's own neighboring listings.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle East Building 3 is one of three buildings on the Intergate East subcampus in Tukwila, part of a larger SDC Seattle campus spanning over a million square feet. The campus totals 54 MW of power capacity across all buildings, but the operator does not publish a figure specific to this building, so its IT load cannot be calculated. Washington state has published capacity figures for only two data center campuses, and this campus ranks third by published megawatts statewide.

The absence of a building-level power specification means this facility's size relative to other AI infrastructure cannot be determined from public sources. The campus as a whole, at 54 MW, is modest compared to hyperscaler campuses now under construction elsewhere, and represents a fraction of the nearly 400 MW Sabey operates across six states. No certifications for this specific building are published.

This campus sits in a Pacific Northwest region where Sabey also operates a second Washington campus powered by hydroelectric generation. Whether Intergate Seattle East Building 3 will matter to AI scaling depends on the operator's tenant decisions and the growth of published capacity on site, neither of which are stated in available sources.
